title: Chipotle Chicken Burrito with Homemade Flour Tortillas
summary: Chewy homemade flour tortillas rolled around chipotle-marinated chicken thigh, bacon-spiked pinto beans, buttery cilantro-lime rice and a simple guacamole.
notes: Video: 'Perfect Chicken Burritos At Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/perfect-chicken-burritos-at-home-recipe (serves 6, prep 30 min, cook 1 hour; the times leave out the dough rest and the optional overnight marinade). The video divides the dough into six tortillas, one per burrito. Where the video and the written recipe differ, the video wins: medium-grain rice (page: basmati, 300 g), juice of 1 whole lime in the rice (page: 1 Tbsp) and about 1/4 onion in the guacamole (page: 3 Tbsp, 30 g). From the written recipe: 1-2 jalapeños (midpoint 1 1/2 used), 2 lb for the six thighs, 15.5 oz cans of beans, 3 large avocados, 1-2 limes in the guacamole (midpoint 1 1/2 used). Our estimates: drained beans 260 g per can; salt in the beans (1/2 tsp kosher), the marinade (1 tsp kosher) and the guacamole (1 tsp kosher), all salted by taste in the video; onion size (USDA medium). The whole marinade is a thick blended paste that stays on the chicken, so it counts in full (house rule). The shallow searing oil stays in the pan with the chicken and counts. The bacon's rendered fat stays in the beans, so raw bacon counts in full. Not counted: bench flour for rolling the tortillas and the splash of water used to rinse the can. Chipotles in adobo have no SR Legacy record (see the new-ingredient note). Lime zest uses USDA lemon peel as a proxy. Assembly amounts are 'as much as you like'; the whole batch of each component is divided over the six burritos.

steps.text: Tortillas: whisk the flour, salt and baking powder, then mix in the warm water and oil by hand. Knead 2-3 minutes until smooth and elastic, cover, and rest 5-30 minutes.
Divide into six balls. On a well-floured counter, flatten each and roll to a thin 12-inch round, about 1/8 inch thick.
Cook each tortilla in a very hot 12-inch cast-iron pan or comal for 15-30 seconds per side, until puffed and lightly charred. Keep warm wrapped in towels.
Beans: finely dice half the onion and thinly slice the garlic and jalapeños (seeding is optional). Cut the bacon into small lardons.
Render the bacon in a cold large pot over medium-low, stirring, 3-4 minutes until crisp and browned. Raise to medium, add the vegetables with a little salt, and sauté about 3 minutes until soft.
Add the rinsed, drained pinto beans, the stock and a little more salt. Simmer until the liquid is reduced by half and everything is hot. Adjust the salt.

Marinade: blend the whole can of chipotles in adobo (rinse the can with a splash of water), the garlic, lime juice and salt, starting low and going to high until very smooth, then stream in the tablespoon of oil. Taste and adjust the salt now.
Massage the marinade into the six boneless, skinless thighs in a bowl. Cook right away or cover and refrigerate overnight.

Heat about 2 Tbsp oil in a heavy 10-12-inch pan over medium-high until just smoking. Lay the chicken in one layer and sear 2-3 minutes per side, then keep turning until it reaches 165°F inside, or finish in a 375°F oven for 5-10 minutes.
Rice: rinse the rice and cook it with an equal volume of water in a rice cooker (or on the stove).

Fluff the hot rice into a large bowl and fold in the kosher salt and softened butter until every grain is coated, then the lime zest, lime juice and cilantro. Taste, then return it to the cooker on keep-warm.
Guacamole: halve, pit, peel and roughly chop the avocados. Salt them generously and mash partway, then add the juice of one lime and mash again, stopping just short of the texture you want.
Taste for salt, then fold in finely chopped onion from the other half (about a quarter onion) and a couple tablespoons of finely chopped cilantro. Finish with more salt and lime to taste.
Take the chicken out of the pan, cut it into 1/2-inch cubes, return it to the warm pan with its juices, toss, cover and keep warm.
Assemble on a hot tortilla: rice in the lower third, then beans, chicken and a generous spoon of guacamole. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly from the bottom.
Optionally wrap each burrito tightly in foil for a couple of minutes to set and steam, then cut in half and serve.
